summary: Bull Point light at the entrance to Sambro Harbour, Nova Scotia: lit 1899 as a wooden tower, replaced by a similar tower in 2016. Coast Guard property; tower closed.

structures.type: square wooden tower with sloping sides and square lantern, painted white
white pyramid tower with red top, vinyl-clad

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. A short walk from parking at the end of Bull Point Road, off NS 349 in Sambro. Site open, tower closed.

events.note: Put in operation 1 December 1899; fixed red light 38 ft (11.6 m) above high water, visible seven miles
Tower built by the department under foreman carpenter McLellan, cost $676.04
Photo-electric switch installed rather than hire another caretaker, when keeper Gilkie was due to retire (LF); NSLPS: automated by 1961
Elevation reduced from 38 to 34 feet between 1966 and 1970; NSLPS says a new tower may have been built then
Deteriorated lantern room removed; watertight mount fitted for the automated light
NSLPS lists fixed green, dated 1990. Its 1922 to 1941 entry gives fixed red. The change is not dated in the sources.
Old wooden tower demolished in late May 2016; a new tower of similar form built in its place

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends spells the first keeper Finlay; the Marine keepers' tables of 1901 and 1910 spell it Findlay. The file uses Findlay, as the Marine tables print it.

The 1899 account gives the tower 33 ft to the lantern vane and the light 38 ft above high water; NSLPS gives the light's elevation as 34 ft after a change dated 1966 to 1970. The 1966 to 1970 change accounts for the difference in the light's height.

The Coast Guard list gives the present tower 8.4 m; the Rowlett directory gives 10 m (33 ft); LF quotes a Coast Guard superintendent calling the new tower slightly larger. The story gives the Coast Guard figure and the Rowlett figure and says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Canadian station, no USLHS roster. The 1899 description (tower, lens, fixed red light, cost, foreman McLellan) comes only from LighthouseFriends quoting the 1899 Marine annual report, which is outside the local corpus (it starts with fiscal 1900). It is unverified against the original. Keeper lines: the 1901 table line ('Findlay, John H Bull Point') and the 1910 table line ('Sambro Haibour Light John H. Findlay Dec. 7, 1.899 . 130 00') are read from OCR; the 1910 salary (130 dollars) is in the same row. Printed page for the 1901 table is not confirmed (scan 260 used). No source names a keeper between about 1923 and 1929. The name Gilkie also appears in the Marine tables at 'Sambro Light and Explosive Signal Station' (Sambro Island, 1905 and 1906 tables). I did not link the two: no source connects them. Lighthouse Digest's 2016 demolition article was not readable (fetch timed out). The Canadian Press article is the only dated 2016 source beyond LF and the directory. The 'weather logs' detail is a community leader's family recollection, reported as her own account. Access: the record says 'unknown'; the Rowlett directory and NSLPS say the site is reachable on foot and the tower closed; suggest 'public' with that note. Chronicling America search 'Sambro Harbour' 'lighthouse' 1899 to 1930: no hits. The record's characteristic 'F G' is the 2020s Coast Guard code (fixed green); the date of the change from red is not in the sources. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1901 table row (Findlay, John H, Bull Point; scan p.260) and the 1911 table row (Findlay, Dec. 7; scan p.259) were matched by column position and were not checked against the page image: the built-in browser refused archive.org. The appointment date now also cites LF's own text (7 December 1899). The statement about the 1923 to 1929 gap now says only what the sources used for the story name.
